aweme_info.desc: DM me the word 'PLATES’ on my IG and I’ll send you my training on how to eat more to lose fat after 35. If you’re a high-performing woman who’s doing everything right and your body still isn’t reacting like it used to, the plate is the first place to look. Why each pick lands where it does: Carbs: Rice on its own digests fast and leaves you hungry again. Oats and potatoes keep your blood sugar steady, so you’re not digging through the pantry at 3pm. Fats: Trail mix is mostly candy and dried fruit, and it disappears fast while you answer emails. Almonds come with fiber and protein. Salmon adds protein and omega-3 fats that keep you full for hours. Drinks: A restaurant margarita can run 300 to 500 calories with a sugar crash on top. Dry white wine and a vodka soda with lime sit around 100 to 120 with no sugar. Alcohol still pauses fat burning, so pick your drink on purpose. Olive oil: A shot on an empty stomach is 120 calories of fat with nothing to keep you full. A tablespoon on your veggies, or a few sprays from a mister, gets you the benefit without the guessing. Lunch: The plain desk salad is usually behind the 9pm pantry raid. Add protein and a real carb and the afternoon changes. Nothing here asks you to eat less. original_client_text.markup_text:
DM me the word 'PLATES’ on my IG and I’ll send you my training on how to eat more to lose fat after 35.

If you’re a high-performing woman who’s doing everything right and your body still isn’t reacting like it used to, the plate is the first place to look.

Why each pick lands where it does:

Carbs: Rice on its own digests fast and leaves you hungry again.
Oats and potatoes keep your blood sugar steady, so you’re not digging through the pantry at 3pm.

Fats: Trail mix is mostly candy and dried fruit, and it disappears fast while you answer emails. Almonds come with fiber and protein. Salmon adds protein and omega-3 fats that keep you full for hours.

Drinks: A restaurant margarita can run 300 to 500 calories with a sugar crash on top. Dry white wine and a vodka soda with lime sit around 100 to 120 with no sugar.

Alcohol still pauses fat burning, so pick your drink on purpose.

Olive oil: A shot on an empty stomach is 120 calories of fat with nothing to keep you full. A tablespoon on your veggies, or a few sprays from a mister, gets you the benefit without the guessing.

Lunch: The plain desk salad is usually behind the 9pm pantry raid. Add protein and a real carb and the afternoon changes.

Nothing here asks you to eat less. The effortless foods fill you up and steady your blood sugar, which lets you eat more while your metabolism rebuilds.

DM me the word "PLATES” on my IG and I’ll send it over.

original_client_text.markup_text:
4 things I wish I knew before losing 100lbs+:

1. It takes WAY longer than you think.
Weight loss isn’t linear, and slow progress is still progress. The version of you who learns to be patient is the version who keeps it off.

2. The boring stuff is what actually changes you.
Meal prep. Walking. Sleeping. Training. Repeating simple habits even when you’re not motivated. There’s no secret. You just have to keep showing up.

3. Your body will fight you sometimes.
Plateaus happen. Your weight will fluctuate. Some weeks the scale won’t move despite doing everything “right.” It doesn’t mean you’re failing. You have to learn to adjust without giving up.

4. Reaching your goal weight doesn’t magically change everything.
You don’t suddenly arrive at the finish line and never struggle again. You still have to choose yourself every day and build a lifestyle you actually want to maintain.

Follow along for fitness, weight loss & lifestyle content 🤍

#weighlossjourney #fitnessjourney #fyp #lifestylecontent #fitnessmotivation

I am using 2kg each dumbbell 👌  You don't need hours in the gym. You need consistency. original_client_text.markup_text:
And honestly? You don't need to wait until January to start.
Save this workout and do it 4× a week using light weights.
I am using 2kg each dumbbell 👌
You don't need hours in the gym.
You need consistency.
And if you combine your workouts with simple nutrition habits, you can make even more progress by Christmas.
🥩 Include protein at every meal — eggs, Greek yogurt, cottage cheese, chicken, fish, lean meat, beans or tofu.
🥦 Fill half your plate with vegetables whenever you can.
🍓 Choose whole foods most of the time and keep highly processed snacks as occasional foods rather than everyday staples.
💧 Drink enough water — thirst can sometimes feel like hunger.
Aim for 4 workouts a week + better food choices + consistency.
Let's see what your body can do by Christmas. ❤️
SAVE this workout and comment 🎄 if you're starting today!
#fullbodyworkout #homeworkouts #burnfat #weightlosss #womenover40

aweme_info.desc: If I had to describe myself before my weight loss, the first thing I need to say is this: I was never overweight👌 My problem wasn’t my weight. My problem was how I was eating, how weak my body felt, and how jelly-like I looked. I had no idea what muscles were or what a truly balanced, nutritious meal looked like! I was stressed, constantly snacking, craving sweets, eating whatever was fast and easy. I was cooking nutritious meals for my kids… while eating random things the entire time. One day I said: this needs to stop🙈 I started with: • 10k steps a day • More protein and fiber (no strict tracking) • Strength training twice a week That’s it. And the difference? Massive. The most important part of this journey was finding recipes I genuinely love. Meals I couldn’t wait to eat. Over time, something incredible happened: my taste completely changed. I don’t crave sweets anymore (and I was a BIG sweet person). I crave homemade food. Vegetables. Nourishing meals🥒🥔🥦🥕🍅🥗 I feel strong. I have muscles. I’m confident in my body. And my immune system? A rock. Not even my kids’ viruses can touch me💪 This wasn’t about losing weight. It was about rebuilding my body.💪

original_client_text.markup_text:
If I had to describe myself before my weight loss, the first thing I need to say is this:
I was never overweight👌

My problem wasn’t my weight.
My problem was how I was eating, how weak my body felt, and how jelly-like I looked. I had no idea what muscles were or what a truly balanced, nutritious meal looked like!

I was stressed, constantly snacking, craving sweets, eating whatever was fast and easy.
I was cooking nutritious meals for my kids… while eating random things the entire time.

One day I said: this needs to stop🙈

I started with:
• 10k steps a day
• More protein and fiber (no strict tracking)
• Strength training twice a week

That’s it.

And the difference? Massive.

The most important part of this journey was finding recipes I genuinely love. Meals I couldn’t wait to eat. Over time, something incredible happened:
my taste completely changed.

I don’t crave sweets anymore (and I was a BIG sweet person).
I crave homemade food. Vegetables. Nourishing meals🥒🥔🥦🥕🍅🥗

I feel strong. I have muscles. I’m confident in my body.
And my immune system? A rock. Not even my kids’ viruses can touch me💪

This wasn’t about losing weight.
It was about rebuilding my body.💪
